data.title: Drug regulator halts obeticholic acid production, orders recall
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- India's apex drug regulator has ordered an immediate halt to the manufacturing, sale, and distribution of obeticholic acid tablets and directed companies to recall the chronic liver disease medication pending a fresh safety review, according to two officials and a document seen by Mint.

The Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi has sought the cancellation of manufacturing licences for obeticholic acid (5mg and 10mg tablets), approved in India in March 2020 to treat primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), following recommendations from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation's (CDSCO) subject expert panel on gastroenterology and hepatology.

The regulator had referred the matter to its gastroenterology and hepatology experts to assess whether obeticholic acid should continue to be sold in India after global regulators, including the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) and the European Medicines Agency, recommended revocation of the drug's authorization due to risks of serious liver injury and a lack of confirmed clinical efficacy.

"Obeticholic acid 5mg/10mg tablets approved by the CDSCO on 11.03.2020 are being marketed in the country for primary biliary cholangitis. However, the European Medicines Agency, in its press release dated 28.06.2024, has recommended that obeticholic acid's marketing authorization be revoked, because its benefits are no longer considered to outweigh its risks," read the 10 November directive.

"The drug has also been withdrawn from the US market after the FDA request dated 12.09.2025. The reasons for withdrawal in the US and the European Union were failure to show efficacy and serious liver injury in some patients," the document said.

The directive also referred to the global assessment of Ocaliva, the drug's innovator brand. "As per the published global regulatory review, the clinical benefits of innovator products have not been confirmed. In particular, study 747-302 failed to show that Ocaliva (innovator) was more effective than placebo (a dummy treatment) in terms of the number of patients whose disease worsened or who died, both in the overall population and in a group of patients with early-stage PBC," the document said.

The regulator added that supplementary evidence did not alter the assessment of the trial outcome. "It was also considered that the data from supportive studies and real-world data were not sufficient to confirm the benefits of Ocaliva and could not counterbalance the negative results of study 747-302," the document added.

Pharmaceutical industry experts questioned the regulatory delay. "Once the USFDA and European Medicines Agency stopped the drug over serious safety risks and even halted clinical trials, what prevented the subject expert committee from acting for more than a year?," asked Uday Bhaskar, former director general at Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India (Pharmexcil).

"While around 10 to 11 manufacturers continued making the API (active pharmaceutical ingredient) and formulations here, stocks remained in the market for patients to consume. Moreover, how effective this recall will actually be across the country remains a big question mark," he added.

Generic versions of obeticholic acid are marketed in India by several companies, including Cipla Ltd, Zydus Lifesciences Ltd, Alkem Laboratories Ltd and Natco Pharma Ltd. Mint's queries sent to the Union health ministry, CDSCO, Cipla, Zydus, and Alkem on Thursday, and to Intercept Pharmaceuticals and Natco Pharma on Friday, remained unanswered.

Medical specialists advised that patients currently on the medication should seek medical evaluation rather than stop treatment without guidance. "The drug can cause severe itching, worsening liver function and, in some patients, serious liver injury, including liver failure. While stopping the medicine does not typically cause withdrawal symptoms, the underlying liver disease, PBC, continues to require treatment and monitoring," said Sharad Malhotra, senior consultant and director, Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare.

He further added that the priority now must be to ensure that affected patients receive timely medical guidance, appropriate alternative therapies and regular follow-up, while strengthening regulatory vigilance to prevent such delays in future.

data.title: Novo Nordisk Secures EU Approval For FREHEMGO In Haemophilia A
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Novo Nordisk (NVO, NOVOB.CO, NOV.DE) has received European Commission marketing authorization for FREHEMGO (denecimig), a next-generation therapy for the routine prophylaxis of bleeding episodes in adults and children with haemophilia A, with or without inhibitors.

The approval marks a significant milestone for the company and expands treatment options for people living with haemophilia A, a rare inherited bleeding disorder caused by a deficiency of clotting factor VIII (FVIII). Patients with the condition face an increased risk of spontaneous and prolonged bleeding, which can lead to joint damage and other serious complications if not adequately controlled.

FREHEMGO is a factor VIIIa mimetic bispecific antibody administered as a subcutaneous injection. Designed to offer greater flexibility and convenience, the therapy can be given once weekly, once every two weeks, or once monthly using a single-use pre-filled pen. The dosing options allow patients and healthcare providers to tailor treatment schedules according to individual needs and preferences.

The European Commission's approval follows clinical data demonstrating the therapy's ability to effectively prevent or reduce bleeding episodes in patients with haemophilia A, regardless of inhibitor status. Inhibitors, which are antibodies that neutralize replacement clotting factors, remain one of the most challenging complications in haemophilia treatment.

Novo Nordisk said it plans to introduce FREHEMGO in the first European markets over the coming year, paving the way for broader patient access across the region.

Beyond Europe, the therapy has already secured approval in Saudi Arabia and remains under regulatory review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other health authorities worldwide. Additional approvals could further strengthen Novo Nordisk's presence in the haemophilia market and expand access to the treatment globally.

NVO closed Friday's regular trading at $41.63 up $0.98 or 2.41%. But in the after-hours trading, the stock dropped $0.19 or 0.46%.

data.title: Zai Lab Announces First-Time Inclusion of KarXT and VYVGART Hytrulo® in China’s 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List, Expanding Access to Key Growth Products
data.description:
Zai Lab Limited (; ), an innovation-driven, global biopharma company, today announced that five of its commercial medicines in China have been included in the country’s 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL). The update includes two first-time listings, expanding patient access to treatments for gMG and schizophrenia, and three renewals, which maintain access across oncology and infectious disease.

Zai Lab Products Newly Added or Renewed in 2026 NRDL:

First-time listings:

  • VYVGART Hytrulo® (efgartigimod alfa, subcutaneous injection): for the treatment of adult patients with anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).

  • KarXT (xanomeline and tropsium chloride capsules): for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.

Renewals:

  • NUZYRA® (omadacycline for injection): for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia and acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections.

  • QINLOCK® (ripretinib tablets): for the treatment of adult patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who have received prior treatment with three or more kinase inhibitors, including imatinib.

  • AUGTYRO® (repotrectinib capsules): for the treatment of adult patients with ROS1-positive locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and adult patients with solid tumors harboring a neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) gene fusion.

“The inclusion of KarXT and VYVGART Hytrulo in the NRDL represents an important milestone for Zai Lab and the patients we serve,” said Dr. Yizhe Wang, Zai Lab Operating Partner. “These listings will help broaden access to two important therapies, including KarXT’s novel mechanism of action for schizophrenia and the convenience of VYVGART Hytrulo’s subcutaneous administration for patients with gMG. Together with the renewal of our other listed products, we are grateful to the National Healthcare Security Administration for its continued support of innovative medicines and remain committed to delivering greater benefit to patients.”

The 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List will take effect on January 1, 2027.

All are indicated for schizophrenia in adults.

data.title: Innovative Immunology Biotech Windward Bio Lists on Nasdaq
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Windward Bio, a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and a clinical-stage biotechnology company, successfully listed on Nasdaq on November 13, 2026. Windward Bio (Nasdaq: WWB) priced its IPO at $17.00 per share. Its shares closed at $28.50 on the first trading day, up 68% from the IPO price, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately $1.69 billion. This is Qiming Venture Partners' 11th IPO in 2026.

Qiming Venture Partners invested in Windward Bio's inaugural Series A financing in 2025 and continued to support the company in its Series B financing in 2026. Qiming also participated in this IPO financing round.

Windward Bio was founded in 2024 with a mission to transform the treatment paradigm for patients living with chronic inflammatory diseases through the development of differentiated biologic therapies targeting clinically validated disease pathways. Led by a team with extensive expertise across discovery, development, and commercialization, Windward Bio is advancing a pipeline of ultra-long-acting antibody medicines to improve clinical outcomes, reduce treatment burden and expand treatment options for patients with serious respiratory and dermatologic diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and atopic dermatitis.

Windward Bio's lead program, WIN378, is a potentially novel anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody engineered for improved potency and extended half-life. WIN378 is currently being evaluated in POLARIS-1, a Phase 2/3 study in severe uncontrolled asthma, and SIRIUS, a Phase 2 study in COPD. The company's pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage, long-acting bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13 with potential applications across multiple inflammatory and immunological diseases. Windward Bio holds exclusive global rights (excluding Greater China and certain Asian countries) to WIN378 through a licensing agreement with Kelun-Biotech and Harbour BioMed, and has separately licensed WIN027 from Qyuns Therapeutics.

"Qiming Venture Partners invests in differentiated, globally competitive biotech innovation designed to address significant unmet needs for patients, and Windward Bio exemplifies this approach. We believe novel, long-acting biologics will reshape the treatment of severe chronic respiratory and skin diseases, and that WIN378 and WIN027 have the potential to expand and meaningfully improve the treatment options available to patients. In the hands of Luca and his team, with their expertise and proven track record, Windward is well-positioned to deliver on this potential, and we look forward to supporting the company through its next phase of growth," said Alexander Sinclair Wilson, Principal at Qiming Venture Partners.

data.title: Tesla Opens Sales Of Autonomous Cybercab For 'Select' Customers — WSJ
data.description:
By Sean O'Kane

Tesla has begun taking orders for personally owned versions of its Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals.

The company said in posts on X on Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990. The vehicle requires a $299-per-month subscription to Tesla's autonomy software and a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit.

The autonomous, two-door vehicle was previously only deployed in Tesla's taxi fleet.

The vehicles are estimated to be delivered in December, according to Tesla's posts.

The announcement comes after Tesla and its Chief Executive Elon Musk spent years promising the company would sell fully autonomous vehicles to regular customers. In 2016, Tesla claimed that all vehicles it was making at the time had the hardware necessary to become fully self-driving. In 2019, Musk predicted Tesla would have "over a million robotaxis" on the roads by the following year.

Those promises have yet to materialize, but Tesla has recently made progress toward its autonomous goals. The company has operated "Robotaxi" versions of its Model Y SUV in Austin, Texas since June 2025. That self-driving ride-hailing service has since expanded to other cities in Texas and Florida.

In September, Tesla started adding Cybercabs to the Austin fleet. The gold, two-seater vehicle has no manual driving controls that are required by federal motor vehicle safety standards.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into whether the Cybercab complies with these regulations. Tesla has told the safety regulator that it believes the Cybercab meets the standards, but the company hasn't publicly explained its position.

Tesla and NHTSA didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The late Friday announcement also signals a possible shift for Tesla's autonomous strategy. On a call with investors in October, Musk said "the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned."

In the social-media posts Friday, the company explained in fine print that the personally owned Cybercabs will only be available to operate "in supported service areas." Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, said in a post that the vehicles will "work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as" the company's existing Robotaxi service.

Tesla's claim that the Cybercab can only be purchased for personal use means buyers won't be able to immediately make money with the vehicle. The company had previously solicited interest in September for "Cybercab fleet vehicle purchasing." Musk has pitched shareholders on the idea that small fleet owners could manage Cybercabs "like a shepherd tends their flock."

Musk has also promised that customers would be able to add their own Teslas to a larger, autonomous ride-hailing network. On Tesla's October call with investors, Elluswamy said this functionality would come in the second quarter of 2027.

data.title: RBI said to allow e-rupee wallets within banking apps to boost adoption
data.description:
Mumbai, Nov. 14 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed banks to integrate digital rupee wallets into their main mobile banking apps, a move aimed at making the central bank's digital currency easier to access and encouraging wider use, according to two people aware of the development.

Until now, banks have offered separate apps for digital rupee wallets. Integrating them into existing banking apps would remove the need for customers to download another application to transact in the central bank digital currency (CBDC), potentially encouraging greater adoption.

"We are planning to integrate this within our app," said one of the bankers cited above. "The main app has a lot of visibility and therefore it would automatically translate into more usage of CBDC."

A CBDC, known in India as the digital rupee (e Rs.), is a digital form of legal tender issued directly by the RBI. It carries the same value as physical currency. Currently, 19 banks offer digital currency wallets. These include Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, State Bank of India, Union Bank and Bank of Baroda, according to RBI data.

"This is definitely beneficial for banks as they do not have to maintain two separate apps. For consumers, it will only make sense if there is more value than using UPI," said Mihir Gandhi, partner and leader, fintech and payments transformation, PwC India.

The RBI launched its retail CBDC pilot in December 2022, initially restricting it to a closed group of participating customers and merchants. In August, RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain told reporters that, since the currency was being used for actual transactions, it could no longer be described as a pilot.

Despite the central bank's expectations for CBDC, transaction volumes remain muted. Retail CBDC in circulation stood at Rs.771.66 crore in FY26, down from Rs.1,016.5 crore in the previous financial year, according to RBI data. In contrast, the value of total banknotes issued-including CBDC-increased from Rs.36.9 trillion to Rs.41.2 trillion over the same period.

An email sent to the RBI seeking comment remained unanswered.

Bankers said the wallets had initially been kept separate because the CBDC was still being tested, and the central bank had not been keen on allowing banks to integrate them into their main apps. With some traction now emerging, the RBI has approved the integration, they said.

"UPI has independent apps (third party) and it is also included in the banking apps. CBDC will also be like this," said the second banker cited above. "It's a very simple utility. You fund the CBDC wallet account from the savings bank account."

The move follows the RBI's decision in 2023 to allow customers to use CBDC wallets to make payments through UPI QR codes. Mint reported in September that while this interoperability gives CBDC access to a large existing merchant-facing infrastructure, the backend processing of such payments by banks and the RBI remains different and requires further work before it can be rolled out at scale.

Experts cautioned that integrating CBDC wallets into banking apps would not necessarily translate into a significant increase in users.

Gandhi of PwC said that although UPI is available on bank apps, most consumers prefer third-party payment applications. "There are so many features packed into a single bank app that customers find it hard to discover, while third-party apps are more focussed," he said.

The RBI has also allowed third-party apps to offer CBDC wallets, but only a handful have adopted the facility so far. Two non-bank platforms, CRED and MobiKwik, launched e-rupee wallets in 2025.

Parijat Garg, an independent fintech expert, said universal QR code acceptance was among the most significant developments for CBDC so far, as it allows customers to use existing UPI QR codes to make payments through their digital rupee wallets.

"Furthermore, if it is now available within the main bank app, of course discovery becomes easy for the consumer and the consumer is most likely to try," Garg said.

He said consumers had adopted UPI Lite partly because it was integrated into the wider UPI ecosystem and enjoyed better acceptance. "Consumers would now have another option to pay when eRupee wallets get integrated," he said.

UPI Lite is a wallet within UPI apps that allows customers to make transactions of up to Rs.1,000 without entering their PIN.

data.title: Hyperliquid Whales Flip Bullish On Bitcoin After Two Weeks of Shorts: Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hyperliquid generated nearly $191 million in third-quarter protocol revenue, according to a quarterly report.
  • Since late August, Circle's USDC reserves' interest has generated half of HYPE's revenue.
  • Payward, Kraken’s parent company, announced plans to launch Bitnomial to run a HIP-3 market on Hyperliquid. 

Hyperliquid’s (HYPE) price edged lower on late Friday as Glassnode data showed the largest traders on Hyperliquid had turned bullish on Bitcoin (BTC) again after two weeks of betting against it.

"Hyperliquid whales just flipped back to the net long on $BTC," Glassnode said on X. The firm said the whales had held short positions over the past two weeks, their first short exposure since early 2026. Glassnode pointed to the group's track record, explaining that the same traders "were short from the top and long through the whole August pump.”

On Stocktwits Hyperliquid was one of the top trending tickers among cryptocurrencies at the time of writing. HYPE’s price was down 2% over the past 24 hours, amid broader market weakness. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HYPE remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

Record Trader Activity

The change in positioning came as Hyperliquid's user base keeps growing, with average daily traders reaching a record 65,161 in the third quarter, up 20% from the previous one, according to a quarterly report from the Hyperliquid Research Collective, an independent research hub that covers the Hyperliquid ecosystem.

Much of that growth came from stock-based contracts, as equity perpetuals recorded nearly $154 billion in third-quarter trading volume, up 161% from the previous quarter. That made equities the largest category on HIP-3, the system that lets outside teams launch their own markets, with 58.8% of its total volume. Korean stocks drove much of the jump, but they also exposed a risk.

A pricing error in the SK Hynix contract on July 28 had triggered over $57 million in liquidations, the report said.

Buybacks Continue, Revenue Rises

Hyperliquid generated close to $191 million in third-quarter protocol revenue, up 21.7% from the previous quarter. About half of that increase came from interest earned on Circle’s (CRCL) USD Coin (USDC) reserves, which began on August 27. The platform's Assistance Fund spent $148.7 million buying HYPE in the quarter, up 5.7%.

However, it bought 26.4% fewer tokens as the average price it paid rose to $72.93. The report also noted Hyperliquid's push into the U.S. Kraken parent Payward announced for Bitnomial, a U.S. regulated derivatives exchange, to run a HIP-3 market on Hyperliquid.

data.title: Indian solar manufacturers look to Germany as China proposes curbs on technology exports
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- China's proposed restrictions on exports of solar manufacturing technologies and equipment have prompted Indian solar manufacturers to look for alternative suppliers, particularly in Germany, amid concerns over the reliability of Chinese supplies, according to three people familiar with the developments.

The proposed curbs may hurt India's ambitious plan to build a domestic solar manufacturing ecosystem, including the projected 100 gigawatts (GW) of capacity for wafers, ingots and polysilicon by the end of this decade. About 30 GW of wafer and ingot capacity is currently in the pipeline. The draft norms cover technology and equipment used in manufacturing polysilicon, thin wafers and advanced solar cells based on TOPCon, heterojunction (HJT), back-contact and tandem processes, according to media reports and executives Mint spoke with.

"The solution is to diversify technology partnerships and strengthen India's domestic manufacturing capabilities,'' said Vineet Mittal, chairman, of clean energy and renewable power conglomerate Avaada Group said in an emailed response.

"Germany and other European countries have strong capabilities in solar manufacturing technology, precision engineering and advanced equipment. We are exploring opportunities across international technology ecosystems, including European equipment manufacturers, engineering specialists and research institutions such as Fraunhofer ISE,'' Mittal said.

"The industry response is already taking shape, with European technology suppliers, particularly from Germany, seeing renewed interest from Indian manufacturers seeking alternatives to turnkey Chinese lines," said Prashant Mathur, chief executive officer of Saatvik Green Energy Ltd. "Companies are actively engaging with suppliers such as Centrotherm and RENA Technologies for advanced cell manufacturing capabilities."

"Indian solar manufacturers are increasingly exploring equipment and technology partnerships across Europe, Japan, Taiwan and other markets, reducing concentration risks," said Amit Manohar, secretary general of the Indian Solar Manufacturers Association (ISMA), an industry body representing integrated solar component manufacturers.

"Germany has a well-established solar equipment and technology base, with several experienced suppliers across key manufacturing processes. European suppliers form an important part of a diversified sourcing approach, ensuring greater supply chain flexibility and long-term manufacturing competitiveness," Manohar said.

However, industry stakeholders caution that Germany may not have the capacity to meet the scale of demand from Indian manufacturers. Sourcing equipment from European suppliers could also come at a 40-50% premium, increasing manufacturing costs and delaying the time taken by Indian companies to break even.

"Any alternatives would inevitably mean a significant increase in costs and project timelines. China dominates the global ingot and wafer manufacturing business, along with the associated supply chain. It is not certain whether any other country would be able to cater to the high demand coming from India," said Vinay Rustagi, chief business officer at solar component manufacturer Premier Energies.

"This development points to the acute need for India to become self-sufficient on the technology front. We are hopeful that Indian machinery suppliers will step up in the medium to long term," he added.

Dilip Mehta, director of engineering, procurement, quality, health, safety and environment (QHSE) at renewable power generator Hexa Climate, said European equipment was more expensive upfront and took longer to deliver. However, when the additional cost is spread across the lifetime output of a manufacturing line, the difference in per-watt cost is relatively small compared with the cost of a wafer or cell.

Manufacturers should focus more on polysilicon availability, yield and production throughput than on the initial equipment price, Mehta said.

"Yield is the real variable. Chinese lines are proven at scale. A new line from any supplier needs time to reach its target yield, so the risk to watch is the ramp-up period, not the sticker price," he said.

The impact on the overall cost of renewable energy projects may also be limited, Mehta said. Modules typically account for less than half of a solar plant's capital expenditure. Their share is even lower in hybrid and firm and dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE) projects that combine solar power with wind and storage.

By Margherita Stancati and Yannis Palaiologos

ATHENS — Garbage bins were set ablaze, stores looted and Molotov cocktails thrown at police, the protesters angry about soaring living costs and deteriorating public services.

These dramatic scenes recently took place in Paris, Milan and other European cities. But they looked a lot like Athens, circa 2010.

At the time, Greek citizens were in revolt against austerity, which came in the form of huge cuts to public spending and suffocatingly high taxes. It was the brutal price to pay for bailout packages that prevented a disorderly default in Greece, and the crisis from spreading to the rest of Europe.

It was the deepest peacetime slump suffered by an advanced economy since the Great Depression, and left it a poorer country to this day. To the rest of Europe it was the kind of cautionary tale that reverberated across the system and fueled anti-EU sentiment — in London, it helped lead to Brexit.

A lot has changed since then. This time around, Europe is burning — but Greece is not.

The Greek economy is growing faster than the European Union average, albeit from a depressed level. At a time of widening deficits and ballooning public debts, the Greek government is one of the few in the West collecting more money than it spends. Greece now borrows more cheaply than France, the U.K. or the U.S.

It is a remarkable turnaround that required a complete rethinking of the state's approach to public finances. It also required a cultural reckoning. Greeks, for better or worse, have learned to expect less from the state than many of their European peers.

They are also more fluent in the language of public finances. They know and care more about budgets and deficits than, say, the average American.

"When I talk to people about the debt, they really seem to listen," Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said in an interview. "People remember the pain. They remember what it means to virtually go bankrupt, what it means to live beyond our means."

While people in Greece broadly understand the limits of state largess, the same can't be said of other parts of Europe, where ideological battles are clashing with financial realities. At stake is the survival of the European social contract, under which citizens long accepted giving up around half of their income in taxes in exchange for cradle-to-grave care.

That model, designed during the period of furious economic growth that followed the World War II, is becoming unsustainable. Aging populations are straining state-funded pension systems, the continent's single biggest spending item. Yet attempts by cash-strapped governments to rein in costs meet fierce popular resistance, with young Europeans rejecting the notion that they will receive fewer benefits than their parents.

As more economies around the world struggle to manage mounting debt and crippling entitlements, Greece may offer a road map for avoiding financial catastrophe.

Watch: Greece's Prime Minister Has Some Advice for the Rest of Europe

TO FIX PUBLIC FINANCES, there needs to be political will. Until the debt crisis, it was in short supply in Greece.

In 1997, a committee chaired by the Greek economist Yannis Spraos issued a report on the pension system that warned it would collapse by 2010. "The sooner corrective measures are taken, the smaller the extent of the necessary correction," the report advised.

Spraos was labeled a doomer. His findings were dismissed by labor unions and he was excoriated by the left-wing press. There is no way the pension system could collapse, argued at the time Christos Polyzogopoulos, then president of the General Confederation of Greek Workers, the country's main labor union. That would only happen as part of "the collapse of the State Budget and the economy as a whole," a scenario thought completely beyond the realm of possibility.

On Jan. 1, 2001 Greece entered the eurozone. That year, Athens's center-left government proposed modest changes to the pension system based on the Spraos report's recommendations such as rising retirement ages and reducing payouts — only to backtrack when the plan triggered mass demonstrations. Nine years later, the Greek state ran out of money. Pension subsidies were the primary culprit.

Spraos is now praised for his foresight. His recent 100th birthday party in Athens was attended by luminaries of the center-left, including the central bank governor.

Greece's public finances were so badly managed at that time that it took months for the government to fully discover how much money it owed. The problem was twofold: in 2009, Greece's budget deficit exceeded 15% of GDP; the previous year, its current-account deficit, a measure of the country's weak trade performance, also topped 15% of GDP. In effect, Greece had been borrowing money to purchase foreign goods.

Tax evasion was rampant, tax collection haphazard and spending on public-sector wages and pensions kept growing. Excess spending to meet pension benefit obligations accounted for 80% of the increase of public debt in the decade between 2001-2010.

Shut out of the markets and its bonds downgraded to junk, Greece was forced to seek assistance from the European Union and the International Monetary Fund. The rescue packages, three in all, came with stringent terms: massive tax increases and deep cuts in public spending.

Salaries fell by over 20% on average. Overnight, the minimum wage was reduced by 22%, from around EUR10,500 to EUR8,200 a year. The retirement age was raised from 65 to 67, and most loopholes for early retirement closed.

The economy shrunk by a quarter. There was widespread material deprivation. Unemployment skyrocketed, especially among the young, many of whom left the country. Formerly middle-class Greeks stood in long lines outside soup kitchens, and could sometimes be spotted scavenging from municipal garbage bins.

The treatment eventually worked. By 2016, Greece turned its budget deficit into a large so-called primary surplus, which excludes debt payments. It has maintained a surplus since, with the exception of the pandemic years. A crackdown on tax evasion, especially on the widespread nonpayment of value-added taxes (VAT), helped boost revenues in recent years.

The Greek government has been disciplined, and a dash populist, in using the extra revenue. It has avoided the bad spending habits of the past, but amid rising costs, it introduced fuel subsidies, it increased the pay of civil servants and raised some pensions. The state also pays one month's rent a year, or up to EUR800, to around one million households. The annual minimum wage is now EUR12,880.

The Greek debt, meanwhile, is under control. It was cut and most of it is now in the hands of European official lenders, with fixed low rates and repayment schedules over several decades. The debt-to-GDP ratio, still the highest in Europe, is rapidly falling and Greece has begun repaying its lenders ahead of schedule.

Dimitrios Tsakonas, the head of Greece's Public Debt Management Agency, played a vital, behind-the-scenes role in making this happen. The crisis transformed the way the state thinks of spending, he said.

"Before the crisis era, the only thing that we really cared about was how to proceed with the funding for the next year," Tsakonas said in an interview.

"You need to think in terms of generations, instead of, say, what is going to happen as far as this year's state budget is concerned, the next elections or even your own lifetime," he said. "You need to be proactive and to have a time horizon that exceeds your lifetime expectancy, period." His agency's debt-sustainability analysis extends to 2070.

THAT SHIFT IN MINDSET has occurred on both sides of the political spectrum. Take former Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras, a left-wing firebrand who used to rail against austerity and brought Greece to the brink of exiting the eurozone in 2015. He ultimately backtracked, signing and successfully implementing his country's third and last bailout package.

Tsipras is the main challenger of Mitsotakis in next year's parliamentary elections. These days, he speaks of fiscal responsibility as a political virtue, reminding would-be voters that his party's economic program is compliant with EU budget rules. Earlier this month, his party, ELAS, became the first to voluntarily present its program to the Hellenic Fiscal Council, a body created during the crisis to monitor Greece's fiscal performance.

"It's part of the legacy of the crisis," says George Houliarakis, a former deputy finance minister under Tsipras. "No one would even consider submitting their economic proposals for assessment to an independent body before 2009."

Not everyone has changed their tune. Yanis Varoufakis, the leather jacket-clad celebrity economist who was Tsipras's finance minister in the tumultuous first six months of his premiership, continues to rage against the policy of high surpluses. But where once he was the most popular politician in Greece, winning the most votes of any candidate in the January 2015 elections, his party is now outside parliament, having failed to clear the 3% threshold required for parliamentary representation.

Most Greek politicians are less likely than in the past to promise benefits they cannot afford — and voters less likely to believe them if they do.

"Our politicians corrupted us to win our votes. We were punished severely for this and we still carry the scars," said Sofia Athanasopoulou, owner of a wine store in Athens's tourist district of Plaka. She said she now understands the social importance of paying taxes. Before the crisis, "we had no tax conscience," she said.

Greece's public finances are in a much better shape, but GDP remains 20% smaller than it was before the crisis. Wages are low. Greece ranks as the second-poorest nation in the EU — ahead of only Bulgaria — in per capita GDP adjusted for purchasing power, according to the World Bank.

data.title: Elon Musk backs call to bring Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
Elon Musk has backed calls to bring Jensen Huang back as Nvidia's chief executive officer (CEO), saying he would sign a petition seeking the former chief's reinstatement. Musk made the remark in response to a post by Yun-Ta Tsai, a senior staff engineer at Tesla Superintelligence, who urged Nvidia employees to use their collective influence to push for Huang's return.

“If NVIDIA employees want Jensen back, they should start with ‘NVIDIA is nothing without its people’ - resign and chill,” Tsai wrote on X.

He argued that experienced graphics processing unit (GPU) engineers are difficult to find and replace, and that employees should take their professional futures into their own hands if they want to influence the company's direction.

“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.”Elon Musk's Reply to Tsai's post

Musk did not identify the petition or share a link to it. His endorsement comes as some Nvidia employees are also calling on the company's board to reconsider Huang's departure.

According to media reports, an internal post on Nvidia's employee suggestion platform, submitted by a longtime engineer before Huang's resignation, has attracted more than 1,600 comments. Several employees have called for Huang to be reinstated, with one anonymous commenter writing: “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss.”

The original post had urged the board to consider employee sentiment before taking a decision on Huang's future. Another employee reportedly sent a company-wide email demanding greater transparency about his exit and expressing support for the former CEO.

Nvidia's chief financial officer, Colette Kress, is currently serving as interim CEO. The company's board has said it will consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent successor.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, November 13, citing people familiar with the matter.

Haas spent seven years at Nvidia, rising to the position of vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013. He is among several candidates being considered, but there is no guarantee that he will be offered the role or accept it, the report said.

Arm declined to comment, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Why did Jensen Huang leave Nvidia?

Nvidia announced on November 12 that Huang had resigned as president, CEO and a member of its board with immediate effect. The decision brought an end to his 33-year leadership of the company, which he co-founded in 1993.

The resignation followed reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a Singapore-based businesswoman whom US authorities suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence. Reports also emerged of relationships involving Nvidia employees.

Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees and took responsibility for his actions. However, Nvidia's official announcement did not specify a reason for his resignation.

The controversy had already prompted the company's board to initiate an independent investigation on November 8, following reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The inquiry is being overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside legal counsel.

In its statement, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe that US national security or the company's trade secrets had been compromised. It added that Huang supported the review and had committed to cooperating with it.

The allegations also brought scrutiny to Nvidia's business dealings in China and the movement of its advanced AI chips. Singapore's authorities said they had investigated Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed International, in connection with suspected irregularities involving chip shipments. Singapore said it had found insufficient evidence of offences, issued her a warning and barred her from returning to the country. The allegations of espionage have not been publicly established.

Nvidia shares face pressure amid leadership uncertainty

Huang's exit has added to concerns about Nvidia's leadership transition and the company's position at the centre of the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on November 12, after declining as much as 14% during the session, and another 3% on Friday, November 13, extending its losing streak to six weeks amid leadership uncertainty.

data.title: What Travelers Caught in the Groundstop Should Know — WSJ
data.description:
By Jacob Passy, Rebecca Cadenhead and Patrick George

Patrick McDonald had already boarded his flight from Los Angeles to New York. But they never took off.

As he deplaned with the rest of his fellow passengers, he went into problem-solving mode to salvage his business trip. But as he purchased a backup flight for Saturday, the price nearly doubled from $500 to $950. When he went to get assistance at a ticket desk in the terminal, he found it empty.

Meanwhile, gate agents warned waiting travelers to grab food while they could. "We're being told every flight on the runway has to evacuate — it's just taking a longer time because the ground crew is spread thin," McDonald said.

For stranded passengers like McDonald, being proactive is the name of the game. As of Friday evening, more than 14,500 flights across the U.S. were canceled or delayed. In the wake of the more than four-hourlong groundstop, airports from coast to coast filled with passengers waiting for word of whether their flights would ever get out. Others were stuck on planes as gate space quickly became limited.

Amy Welton and Chuck Hawks were at the airport rental-car counter in Newark, N.J., debating whether to rent cars and drive home to Omaha, Neb., and Phoenix, respectively. The two are co-workers who were in town for training.

Welton said she was in the boarding line when she started getting texts from friends asking about the groundstop. They were then told to leave the line and that an update would come at 6 p.m. Then: "Your update is we have no update," she recalled.

"I just want to go home," she said. "I don't want to sit in an airport and wait."

Here's what travelers should do if they are stuck on the ground:

Put your phone to work

Lines at airline ticket desks, hotel concierges and rental-car counters are sure to be long. While waiting, whip out your phone.

Airlines including Delta, United and Alaska issued waivers to allow travelers to change plans without paying a difference in fare. Alaska Airlines said travelers could also cancel and get a refund. Delta was offering refunds in the form of credits for future flights.

The fastest approach will be to make use of the mobile app to request changes. Flights in the coming days will sell out, so the sooner you act, the better. Also consider reaching out to the carrier via X or other social-media platforms.

If you feel more comfortable talking to a real person rather than a chatbot, try to contact the airline via its international hotline rather than the domestic phone number, because wait times can be shorter.

Go into the conversation prepared with details for other flights you're open to taking, and avoid itineraries that include layovers to reduce the chances of more disruption to your plans.

If you can't make it to your destination in time for the reason you were traveling, ask airline representatives about the company's "trip-in-vain" policies. When triggered, these policies can provide you with refunds that might not be offered due to an extensive delay since the situation is beyond the airline's control.

Put your points to use

Most carriers have eliminated fees tied to redepositing points if you choose to cancel your plans, so using points or miles can be a good way of hedging your bets for backup flights. Keep in mind, refunds might not be possible for fares booked in basic economy, and make sure to cancel award tickets, which are booked using rewards, before the scheduled departure to get a refund.

Plus, using points can help you to save in the event that the cost of booking another flight or hotel is higher last minute.

Download airport apps

If you haven't done so already, make sure you have the app for your local airport saved to your phone. As hubs fill with passengers from delayed or canceled flights, airport authorities may advise those with departures later in the day to stay home.

For instance, at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, security officers warned against going through TSA checkpoints because of the crowds on the other side.

Check with your credit-card company

Many premium cards come with travel-insurance benefits that can cover you for travel booked with that card. They may provide additional assistance beyond what an airline can do, such as booking seats on flights with other airlines or finding options for hotels.

If you plan to file any travel-insurance claims related to the groundstop, be sure to document any expenses. Take photos of itemized receipts for meals, hotels, ground transportation and anything else you might need to purchase as a result of the situation to get your money back.

Don't abandon your luggage

If the groundstop has caused you to rethink your travel plans entirely and you checked a bag, don't just leave the airport assuming your bags won't be flown to the destination.

Inform an airline representative of your plans, and ask them if your luggage can be pulled. If so, they may send it to their office near baggage claim where you can retrieve it. Or they may ask for an address the bags can be sent to.

If you have a flight Saturday, prepare ASAP

As of Friday evening, airlines had already canceled hundreds of flights. While the groundstop has been lifted, it could take time for airline operations to recover. For those with flights in the days ahead, being prepared can prevent a lot of frustration.

In your carry-on luggage, pack food, a change of clothing and any essential medications to have on hand in case you're delayed. Make sure to leave your house with your phone fully charged — and have a way to charge it in the airport.

If you're considering alternate ways of getting to your destination, act fast

At Chicago O'Hare International Airport, there were long lines at the rental-car desks.

Jonathan Vizcaino and Ashleigh Dodero's flight back to San Diego, where they live, was delayed, then canceled. Neither think they'll be able to fly out of O'Hare Saturday, either. They thought they could do a cross-country, 30-hour drive home.

"I waited in line for a car for 45 minutes," Vizcaino said. But when he got to the front of the line there were no reservations left.

Vizcaino and Dodero, both real-estate agents, had traveled to Chicago for work and stayed an extra day to watch a hockey game.

"We wanted to be tourists in Chicago for one day, and now it seems like we'll be tourists here for a while," Dodero said.

Write to Jacob Passy at jacob.passy@wsj.com, Rebecca Cadenhead at rebecca.cadenhead@wsj.com and Patrick George at patrick.george@wsj.com

data.title: Trump official seeks $50 billion for air traffic control after outage
data.description:
By David Shepardson

The Trump administration boosted its request for air traffic control funding to $50 billion late Friday after a communications issue forced a nationwide groundstop that halted thousands of flights for hours.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and the White House earlier on Friday asked for $30.1 billion to upgrade the United States' aging airports and air traffic control system.

"This is an emergency," Duffy said. "What's more important than having an air traffic control system that actually works?"

The issue impacted the FAA's en route centers that handle traffic between airports. But the Republican-led Senate Commerce Committee said the incident highlights the need to prioritize modernizing those centers over other projects and noted Congress approved $1.9 billion to replace outdated en route centers.

The world's most complex airspace has experienced a series of events in recent years that have disrupted flights and risked safety. In January 2025, a midair collision at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport killed 67 people.

Congress already approved $12.5 billion over five years in July 2025 to upgrade air traffic control and increase the hiring of controllers following complaints about airport ​congestion, flight delays and technology ​problems.

The request from White House Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy seeks $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernization, including $7.2 billion for a common automation platform and controller workstations and $2 billion for cloud computing.

"This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace - delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure," Duffy and Vought wrote to lawmakers asking for swift action.

Major airlines including American Airlines , Delta Air Lines , United Airlines and Southwest Airlines have expressed support for the request.

The $30.1 billion request also includes $2 billion to replace and improve Federal Aviation Administration air traffic control towers and $18 billion for airport-related projects including $10 billion to modernize or replace aging terminals.

The FAA relies on decades-old ​computers as well as replacement parts bought through auction websites. Last week, it said it would replace by the end of 2028 floppy disks used for weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic control facilities.

Vought and Duffy in their letter said the FAA has replaced 68% of legacy copper telecommunications network with high-speed fiber infrastructure.

The administration has called for the Republican-led Congress to approve funding in the final weeks of the year. Democrats are set to take control of Congress in January.

In September, the dual failures of a circuit at a Philadelphia ​air traffic facility and the ​accidental severing of a ⁠fiber-optic cable in New Jersey by a construction crew led to thousands of flights across the densely populated Northeast being delayed or canceled.

data.title: Airlines aim to get passengers on their way as ground stop lifted
data.description:
Key points:
  • A nationwide ground stop at all US airports that began around 4p ET and ended around 8p ET is over, but the impact on stranded passengers could take days to fix.
  • JetBlue Airways said it was cancelling all flights scheduled for Friday night, except for Europe-bound departures. 
  • United Airlines said it is " cancelling a significant number of Friday evening flights" and American Airlines said that "teams across American are working to safely get additional flights moving and customers on their way as conditions allow." Earlier, the airline said it will "be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible."
  • While the ground stop was in effect, Southwest said it was "making operational adjustments across our network in compliance with the nationwide groundstop."
  • All airlines appear to be waiving change fees. 
  • Around 1.5 million people are impacted by flight cancellations, based on analysis from Cirium.

data.title: Biocure Technology Inc. Provides Update on Transaction to Acquire Glorious Success Limited
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

VANCOUVER, British Columbia – TheNewswire - November 13, 2026 - Biocure Technology Inc. (“CURE” or the “Company”) (CSE: CURE) announces, further to its press release dated August 12, 2026, that it has entered into an amendment dated November 10, 2026 (the “Amendment”) to the definitive share exchange agreement dated August 11, 2026 (the “Share Exchange Agreement”) with Glorious Success Limited (“GSL”) pursuant to which Company will acquire all of the issued and outstanding securities of GSL (the “Transaction”).

The Amendment adjust the aggregate consideration due for the currently outstanding shares of GSL (the “GSL Shares”) from 12,459,091 shares of CURE following completion of the Transaction (the “Resulting Issuer”) to 11,325,464 shares of the Resulting Issuer. In addition the Amendment extends the outside date for completion of the Transaction and related concurrent financing from December 31, 2026 to January 31, 2027. All other terms of the Transaction remain the same.

GSL is a Hong Kong holding company and the sole shareholder of Idea Paragon Inc., a South Korea-based mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion and sports media company operating as Black Combat.

Trading in the common shares of the Company is currently halted in accordance with the policies of the CSE and will remain halted until such time as all required documentation in connection with the Transaction has been filed with and accepted by the CSE and permission to resume trading has been obtained from the CSE.

Transaction Summary

Pursuant to the Share Exchange Agreement as amended by the Amendment, the Company will consolidate its existing share capital on the basis of a ratio determined by the price of GSL securities in the Private Placement (as defined below) divided by a deemed value of $0.134 (the “Consolidation”), currently expected to result in a consolidation ratio equal to approximately 16.42 old shares for one new common share (the “Resulting Issuer Shares”). As outlined above, pursuant to the Amendment, as consideration for the currently outstanding shares of GSL (the “GSL Shares”), the Company will issue an aggregate of 11,325,464 Resulting Issuer Shares.

No finder’s fees are payable in connection with the Transaction. Each of Collin Kim, Konstantin Lichtenwald and Steven Pearce will be entitled to receive a bonus for their services to the Company in association with the Transaction, equivalent to 250,000 Resulting Issuer Shares each.

The Transaction remains subject to a number of terms and conditions, including, but not limited to, the completion of additional due diligence, the completion of the Consolidation, the completion of the Private Placement as further described below, the completion of the Debt Settlement as further described below, the approval of the shareholders of the Company, and the approval of the CSE and other applicable regulatory authorities.

Private Placement

Pursuant to the Share Exchange Agreement, it is a condition of the Transaction that GSL complete a private placement for aggregate gross proceeds of at least $3,090,000 at a price of $2.20 per GSL Share (the “Private Placement”). GSL Shares issuable pursuant to the Private Placement will be exchanged for Resulting Issuer Shares on a one for one basis.

Cash finder’s fees of 8% of the proceeds raised are expected to be payable in connection with the Private Placement.

The Resulting Issuer intends to use the net proceeds of the private placement to fund the Transaction, to develop its business and for working capital.

This news release does not constitute an offer to sell and is not a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities in the United States. The securities of the Company and GSL have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “U.S. Securities Act”) or any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to U.S. Persons unless registered under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable state securities laws unless pursuant to an exemption from such registration.

Debt Settlement

As conditions of the Transaction, the Company intends to settle approximately $300,000 in debt (the “Debt Settlement" owed to various parties through the issuance of pre-Consolidation common shares of the Company at a price of $0.134 per share (the “Settlement Shares”), subject to the approval of the CSE. Portions of the indebtedness are expected to be settled with members of the Company’s management team and will constitute a “related party transaction” as defined in MI 61-101. The Settlement Shares will be subject to applicable resale restrictions under securities laws.

Board of Directors of Resulting Issuer

Upon completion of the Transaction, the board and management of the Resulting Issuer shall be reconstituted to comprise:

Pyounghwa Park – Director and Chief Executive Officer

Prior to founding Black Combat, Mr. Park was the Director and Founder of Chromatic Film, where he produced a range of mixed martial arts documentaries that laid the creative foundation for Black Combat’s unique brand identity. In addition to his executive role, Mr. Park is also a professional mixed martial arts fighter within the Black Combat Universe, currently holding the Underground King Title. His personal success in the ring and the popularity of his matches were pivotal in the creation and early growth of the organization.

Jongeon Lim – Director and President

Mr. Lim brings a multidisciplinary background in healthcare, corporate leadership, and media entrepreneurship. Prior to co-founding Black Combat, Mr. Lim served as CEO of ADM Korea Inc., a publicly listed company on the KOSDAQ, and practiced medicine at Mojelim, one of Korea’s leading plastic surgery clinics. His passion for marketing and strategic business development played a central role in launching Black Combat alongside Mr. Park. In his current capacity, Mr. Lim is responsible for strategic partnerships and business development, spearheading collaborations with companies such as My Music Tastes and Sidus to amplify the brand’s reach. He also leads investor relations and contributes medical expertise to the organization, ensuring the well-being and performance readiness of its athletes

Jong Yun Choi – Director

Mr. Choi holds a degree in Business from Oklahoma State University and previously worked as a valuation specialist at Yuanta Korea. He is currently the CEO of DEA TI Co., a Kosdaq-listed company in Korea, as well as the CEO of The Nice Music Group, a hip-hop label. Leveraging his experience in both venture capital and large-scale enterprises, he oversees business transactions to ensure corporate transparency.

Anthony Wong – Director

Mr. Wong is an accomplished senior executive and board director with extensive experience in corporate governance, financial oversight, strategic transactions, and international business across publicly listed companies in Canada, Singapore, and Hong Kong. Mr. Wong is a Member of the Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada and the Institute of Chartered Accountants of British Columbia.

Sang Goo (Collin) Kim – Director

Mr. Kim has been involved in various mineral projects bringing together Canadian and major Korean companies as well as involved in several listing transactions where Korean companies were successfully listed in the Canadian stock exchanges. Mr. Kim is a Vice President for Columbia Capital Inc. since 2008 and has been a director of First Atlantic Nickel Corp., a Canadian junior exploration company since 2015 until his recent resignation in May 2025. He worked for Hanwha Corp. one of Korean business conglomerates for 16 years including five years as a Chief Representative of Hanwha’s Jakarta office, dedicating himself to trading business.

Konstantin Lichtenwald – Chief Financial Officer

Mr. Lichtenwald is a Canadian CPA, CGA and an ACCA in the UK and has over 17 years of corporate finance experience, including experience in accounting, financial management, compliance, M&A, reverse takeovers and initial public offerings. He has lived and worked in multiple jurisdictions including Germany, Australia, USA and Canada. He is a director of a number of private and publicly listed companies in Canada. Mr. Lichtenwald holds a Bachelor of Business from Pforzheim University located in Germany.

Shareholder Meeting

data.title: U.S. Flights Resume After FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop, But Delays Persist
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Air travel across the United States began returning to normal after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop that had halted domestic departures for more than four hours following a major telecommunications outage.

The unprecedented disruption affected airports across the country, leaving thousands of flights delayed or canceled and creating widespread uncertainty for airlines, passengers and airport operators. The outage impacted communications at multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, prompting the FAA to temporarily stop departing flights nationwide while technicians worked to identify and resolve the issue.

'The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,' the agency said, adding that its technicians were investigating the source of the disruption.

Following restoration of critical communications systems, the FAA lifted the ground stop and authorized flights to resume operations. However, aviation authorities warned that delays and schedule disruptions are expected to continue as airlines work through significant backlogs and reposition aircraft and crews.

The impact extended beyond the United States, with U.S.-bound flights departing from major airports across the Asia-Pacific region also affected by the temporary halt. Airlines operating transpacific routes were forced to adjust schedules, delay departures or hold aircraft pending further guidance from U.S. authorities.

The disruption underscores the aviation sector's reliance on stable communications infrastructure, as even brief outages can ripple through the highly interconnected air traffic system. Industry observers noted that recovery from large-scale ground stops often takes several hours after restrictions are lifted, particularly at major airline hubs.

While flight operations have resumed, passengers are being advised to check the status of their flights before heading to the airport, as carriers continue to manage delays and cancellations caused by the outage.

The FAA said it will continue investigating the telecommunications issue and provide further updates as more information becomes available.

How to Make the Most of Rising Bond Yields — Barron's
data.description:
Mary Ellen Stanek, Baird's chief investment officer emeritus, sees value in financial-company bonds, higher-quality municipals.

By Debbie Carlson

Bonds offer investors some of the most attractive yields in decades on a nominal and an inflation-adjusted basis, says Mary Ellen Stanek, managing director and chief investment officer emeritus at Milwaukee-based Baird Advisors.

With 47 years of fixed-income investment management experience under her belt, Stanek should know.

Bonds may experience volatility due to uncertainty about inflation, the interest-rate outlook, and other macroeconomic issues, but investors shouldn't be afraid to lock in current yields, she says.

Baird manages $195 billion across 10 taxable and municipal bond funds, all rated highly by Morningstar. Stanek is a named portfolio manager on the firm's five taxable bond funds. She spoke with Barron's on Oct. 20 and Nov. 3 about her economic and bond market outlook and corporate and municipal credits that the Baird team likes now.

An edited version of the conversation follows.

Barron's: How should investors approach bonds if they are worried that rates will rise further?

Mary Ellen Stanek: It depends on your objective. If you have near-term liquidity needs and you're more risk-averse, you don't have to take very much duration risk to earn relatively high yields. [Duration is a measure of a bond's interest-rate sensitivity that factors into its yield and maturity.] For longer-term investors, there is good value in bonds in the intermediate part of the [yield] curve. That is where our Baird Aggregate Bond fund and Baird Core Plus Bond fund durations are. They're in the high five-to-six-year duration range.

We are finally getting real yields after adjusting for inflation. In the third quarter, the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate Bond Index's inflation-adjusted yield — the index yield minus the core Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — was 3.2%.

The Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady at its October meeting after raising rates in September for the first time in more than three years. What is the outlook for rates now?

I think rates will stay higher. It wasn't a surprise to see them on hold in October. We view that as more of a pause with a bias to another quarter-percentage-point hike later this year or early in 2027. It depends on crude oil prices and the inflation outlook.

Rates are attractive and are going to stay attractive. You don't want to run away from bonds, not at these valuations. The rhetoric out there can be pretty negative about volatility in the bond market.

Here's another way to look at it. At the end of the third quarter, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was 5.29% and the S&P 500 earnings yield, the reciprocal of the price-to-earnings ratio, was 3.81%. The last time the Treasury yield was that high was in 2002. This is a longer-term trend.

It is just another reason to at least pay attention to bonds and consider owning them.

What is your outlook for the economy?

The economy continues to surprise on the upside. Artificial-intelligence/data center spending has boosted gross domestic product readings, but consumer spending overall has also remained strong. We are concerned that the top 20% of U.S. consumers account for 60% of spending, while the bottom 80% account for 40%. If asset levels soften — that is, if stocks fall — and strong household net worth weakens, consumer spending could fall. But spending looks to remain pretty steady into 2027.

We are late in the credit cycle, but corporate-credit fundamentals are still solid, and strong flows into the bond market are keeping spreads [between corporate and Treasury yields] relatively tight. Spreads have widened a bit recently, as excessive optimism is softening with a bit of re-evaluation of market risk.

How are you managing portfolios to reflect your positive view on bonds?

We continue to think there is value in well-diversified, triple-B-rated exposure, and we are trying to keep duration generally more short to intermediate in the Aggregate Bond fund and Core Plus fund. In Core Plus, 27.3% of the portfolio is triple-B exposure versus the Bloomberg U.S. Universal Index's 13.1%. In the Aggregate Bond fund, it is 21.4% versus the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate benchmark, which is at 11.5%.

In Core Plus, we are underweight below-investment-grade versus the benchmark. We don't think the value is as compelling there. In both funds, our weighting in financials is double that of the funds' respective indexes. There is good value in financials.

Which credits have you bought, and why?

We like Barclays Bank. It's a solid bank based in the United Kingdom, with a credit rating between high-triple-B and A, depending on the ratings agency. It has good earnings and capital. We bought five-year and 10-year bonds, with 10-years being the cheapest. The 10-year bonds yielded 1.43 percentage-point above U.S. Treasuries, an attractive spread.

Another name we like is Western & Southern Life Insurance. It is a high-quality life-insurance company, with a high-quality credit rating in the low-double-A range. We bought three-year funding-agreement-backed notes [bonds backed by insurance contracts] at a 0.65 percentage-point spread above the three-year Treasury. The notes rank at the policyholder level, a senior-ranking claim above ordinary corporate debt.

What is another favorite credit?

HCA Healthcare is the largest for-profit hospital chain and health system in the U.S., with its biggest footprint in Texas and Florida. We bought seven-year bonds, priced at a spread of 1.05 percentage points above the seven-year U.S. Treasury note. The credit rating is investment grade, mid-triple-B. [The debt] has durable demand in any economic cycle.

You are keen on municipal bonds. Why?

Munis have compelling value. Baird Municipal Bond fund has a yield of 4.86%. But the tax-adjusted yield is 8.21% for someone at the top tax rate of 40.8% [37% federal income tax plus the 3.8% net investment income tax]. An 8% tax-adjusted yield by historic standards is very attractive. Even for the Baird Short-Term Municipal Bond fund, which carries about a 21/2-year duration, yields at 4.12% imply a 6.96% tax-adjusted yield.

When you tax-adjust municipal bond yields, they are a particularly good relative value. We aren't saying that the equity market won't keep going [up], but [the bond market] is getting competitive for the marginal investment dollar.

What muni credits do you like?

Thematically, we have been trying to buy higher-quality issuers, those with longer call protection [the period when the issuer isn't allowed to redeem the bond early] to "lock in" yields for a longer time. We like general obligation bonds.

We like school districts. Warren Township Metropolitan School District in Indiana is one. The school district has an A-plus rating, and is part of the Indiana State Intercept Program, giving it an enhanced double-A-plus rating. [Under the program, the state will pay bondholders directly if the district is unable to, giving the bonds a higher rating.] The bonds maturing in July 2045 pay a 5.25% coupon and aren't callable until July 2036. The bonds were priced at $102.271 at new issue, and the yield to call was 4.95%. [Yield to call is the annualized return until the first call date and the payoff is the call price.]

How about another name?

The Alabama State Toll Road Bridge & Tunnel Authority has an Aa3/AA rating, with backing from the Alabama Transportation Department. We bought a 5.25% bond maturing in January 2051 and it is callable in January 2037. The bonds were priced at $100.942 at new issue and the yield to call was 5.13%. The proceeds help finance a bridge to replace an existing tunnel on Interstate 10 through Mobile, Ala.

Your early skepticism about data-center debt was prudent. What are your current thoughts?

Initially we were cautious because we thought the structures weren't in line with investors' interests. You have to look at each of the underlying credits to understand what the credit story looks like. You have to look at the structure of the security and do the obvious "what-if" scenarios. Not all of these projects are going to be successful. You want to make sure that you're disciplined about how you're getting exposure, and are you being paid to take it?

The AI buildout has been supporting the economy. What happens if that spending slows?

If it slows, it will probably be a gradual slowing, rather than something that stops suddenly. A gradual slowing could help with inflation or at least stop the rise in inflation.

The other thing to keep in mind is that the One Big Beautiful Bill Act allowed immediate expensing provisions for U.S. businesses. That was intentional. It was supposed to kick up economic activity and particularly a lot of capital projects to reshore production and bring supply chains to the U.S.

Anecdotally we have heard that the buildout is drawing in resources competitively, so if AI spending slows, will other capital project plans then take priority? Will the labor and resources just shift to some of those plans?

You have been a fixed-income investor for 47 years. Does the current environment remind you of anything else in your career?

I wouldn't say cycles repeat exactly, but there are patterns you recognize that give you conviction that you're on the right track directionally. In the past 15-20 years, below-normal interest rates fueled a lot of things, including a repricing of risk in some areas. Savers were hurt.

Now it is the opposite. We are starting to see strong demand for bonds. It is something we watch carefully because of all the debt that has been issued. We believe the strong demand is reflective of the value that investors see with nominal and real interest rates at attractive levels. Bonds are playing their traditional role.

Thanks, Mary Ellen.

data.title: How to Help Consumers: Credit-Card Rate Caps — Barron's
data.description:
By Randall W. Forsyth

Affordability, or the lack thereof, was the issue motivating voters in the midterm elections. Politicians clearly heard voters' voice but now comes the question of what to do about it. Energy prices are unlikely to come down soon to levels prevailing before the Iran war. Tariffs are unlikely to be reversed, and even if they were, it would do little to bring down the cost of housing or medical care.

But there is one price that can be lowered to bring relief to Americans' stressed budgets: credit card interest rates. "The cost of money is part of the cost of living," as an NBER working paper put it last year. Even though it's not counted in measures such as the consumer price index, the cost of credit has weighed heavily on consumer sentiment.

This is a rare issue that has support across the wide political divide in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the Massachusetts Democrat who is likely to head the Senate Finance Committee in the next session, said on CBS' Face the Nation this past Sunday that she was ready to work with President Donald Trump on his proposal to cap credit card interest rates at 10%.

With credit-card balances hitting a record $1.29 trillion in the third quarter, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, a cap on interest rates on plastic surely would resonate with a public now paying an average of 21.19% on an average balance of $6,678.

Not only are 20%-plus credit-card rates high absolutely, they are high relative to other market-determined interest rates. Two decades ago, when the Federal Reserve's federal funds target was over 5%, credit card rates averaged under 14%. Now, with the 3.88% midpoint of the Fed's target range for its policy rate, plastic costs half again as much as 20 years ago.

Critics contend capping credit-card rates will mean less credit for riskier borrowers with low credit scores. A New York Fed paper published this past June came to that conclusion.

Other analyses found capping card rates may mean a hit to banks' profit margins. Another New York Fed paper found credit-card lending generated a return on assets more than four times the banking sector's overall ROA.

These fat profit margins leave plenty of room to lower card rates without curtailing credit to lower-rated borrowers, according to a study last year by Brian Shearer, director of competition and regulatory policy at Vanderbilt University. In fact, the majority of revenue for banks issuing cards actually come from "interchange" fees paid by merchants.

Shearer estimated that rate ceilings of 10% (as proposed by Trump and backed by Warren) would save consumers $100 billion a year. The benefit would accrue mostly to those with lower FICO scores (under 600), although it may cut lending and reduce rewards. But card issuers also could cut expenses, especially advertising.

Alternatively, a 15% cap would save consumers an estimated $48 billion annually, with no expected adjustments to lending volumes or rewards. An 18% cap saves just $16 billion, with top-grade borrowers possibly actually paying more if all banks moved to the ceiling rate, Shearer concluded.

While it's a rare issue that garners support from both parties in today's highly partisan Washington, past proposals to cap credit card interest have drawn objections from the formidable banking lobby. Still, it's an issue for consumers and investors to watch in the new year.
